sentences.text:
HON'BLE MS. JUSTICE TARA VITASTA GANJU  ORDER % 08.07.2025 CM Appl.39476/2025[Exemption from filing certified copies]
1. Allowed, subject to just exceptions.
2. The Application stands disposed of.
MAC.APP. 413/2025 & CM Appls.39475/2025[Stay] and 39477/2025[Seeking permission to lead additional evidence]

3. The present Appeal has been filed under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 impugning the award dated 30.01.2025 passed by the learned Presiding Officer, MACT-02, Tis Hazari Courts,
Delhi [hereinafter referred to as "Impugned Award"].

By the Impugned Award, the compensation in the sum of Rs. 34,69,523/- along with 9% interest per annum has been granted to the Respondent Nos. 2 and 3/Claimants [since Respondent No.1 has already passed away].
4.

The only challenge raised by the Appellant in the present Appeal is to the non-grant of recovery rights in view of the fact that the driver of the offending vehicle did not have a valid and effective driving license with an This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 10/07/2025 at 21:39:12 endorsement for driving a vehicle carrying hazardous goods.

5. Learned Counsel for the Appellant submits that although an averment was made to this effect in its written statement filed before the learned Tribunal, no evidence was led by the Appellant which has led to the non- grant of recovery rights.

sentences.text: Learned Counsel for the Appellant also submits that he also wishes to lead additional evidence and an appropriate Application for the same has already been filed.
6. Issue Notice on this limited ground.
Learned Counsel for Respondent Nos. 2 and 3 accepts Notice.
On steps being taken, let Notice be issued to Respondent No. 4 & 5 via all modes.
An affidavit of service be filed within two weeks.

6.1 Learned Counsel for Respondent Nos. 2 and 3 points out that Respondent No. 1 has been deleted in terms of the order passed by the learned Tribunal on 30.01.2023 and that the memo of parties as filed with the present Appeal is incorrect.
6.2 Learned Counsel for the Appellant shall file an amended memo of parties within a week.
7. Subject to the deposit of entire decretal amount inclusive of up-to-date interest within a period of 6 weeks, the operation of the Impugned Award shall remain stayed till the next date of hearing.
In the event, there is any default in depositing the amount, the interim protection granted by this Court shall automatically stand vacated.

7.1 Learned Counsel for the Respondents/Claimants submits that since there is no challenge to the quantum of the Appeal, the Respondents/Claimants may be permitted to withdraw the entire decretal This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 10/07/2025 at 21:39:12 amount.

7.2 Accordingly, upon deposit by the Appellant, 85% of the deposited amount inclusive of up-to-date interest shall be released to the Respondents/claimants in accordance with scheme, as is set out in the Impugned Award.
8. The Registry is directed to place on record the digital copy of the Trial Court Record duly paginated and book-marked in accordance with the rules of the High Court.
9. Replies to the pending Applications be filed within a period of six weeks.
9.1 Rejoinder(s), if any, be filed within a period of four weeks thereafter.

10. List before the concerned Registrar for completion of service and pleadings on 24.09.2025.
11.
The parties will act based on the digitally signed copy of the order.
TARA VITASTA GANJU, J JULY 8, 2025/r
